markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the seasonally adjusted number of total nonfarm job openings in the United States for October 2026 is above 7.30M, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Underlying is the seasonally adjusted number of total nonfarm job openings for October 2026, as reported in the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) scheduled for release on Dec 1, 2026.

Job openings are measured on the last business day of the reference month and are reported by BLS in thousands. For purposes of this market, values expressed in millions will be converted directly from the BLS-reported value in thousands. For example, a reported value of 7,350 thousand is equivalent to 7.350 million.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the U.S. Census Bureau reports that U.S. private data center construction spending for October 2026 is above $90.0B (billion) at a seasonally adjusted annual rate, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market will resolve based on the first published estimate of U.S. private data center construction spending for October 2026 reported by the U.S. Census Bureau in its Value of Private Construction Put in Place – Seasonally Adjusted Annual Rate data.

The relevant figure is found under:

Private → Nonresidential → Office → Data center

The Census Bureau reports this figure in millions of dollars at a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR). For example, $70 billion corresponds to $70,000 million.

The first figure published for the relevant month will be used, including if Census identifies that figure as preliminary. Subsequent revisions, corrections, or updated estimates will not affect the market’s resolution.

An Emergency Directive counts once CISA has published it on its Cybersecurity Directives page. It need not name CVE-2026-109618 or CVE-2026-109619, but its required actions must cover those vulnerabilities in PHP, such as requiring agencies to patch, mitigate, inventory or remove affected PHP systems.

A new version of an existing Emergency Directive counts only if that version itself adds required actions covering these vulnerabilities.

The following do NOT resolve this market to YES:
A Binding Operational Directive.
A supplemental direction to an existing Emergency Directive.
An addition to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and any remediation deadline that follows from one.
A CISA alert, advisory or other guidance urging agencies or the public to patch.
A statement that an Emergency Directive is under consideration or forthcoming.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the executive action is issued.
markets.expiration_value: No
markets.rules_primary: If Donald Trump has taken any signed executive action renaming any ocean after Issuance and before Nov 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The qualifying action must be of the specific type designated (executive order, presidential memorandum, proclamation, directive, determination, or finding), be signed by the President personally during the specified time period, and explicitly address the topic in the document's operative provisions, title, or official White House summary. Actions must have legal or policy effect - ceremonial proclamations without policy impact do not qualify unless specifically included. Actions that only incidentally mention the topic, statements without formal action, actions by cabinet members, legislative proposals without executive action, and signing statements do not qualify. The action must be publicly announced or documented by a Source Agency before expiration.

Ocean means the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian, Arctic, or Southern Ocean. The action must adopt or direct adoption of a different name for United States official use; renaming only a gulf, sea, bay, or lake does not qualify. An action covering only the portion of an ocean within United States jurisdiction qualifies. Adoption by other countries or an international body is not required.

markets.rules_primary: If Laurent Nuñez leaves as Interior Minister of France before Dec 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market resolves based on when the departure is publicly announced or officially communicated, regardless of the effective date.

If the person leaves the role due to death (i.e., if the person dies while holding the role), all contracts on the person may resolve to the last fair price as determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange. Temporary leaves of absence, suspensions, or recusals do not constitute leaving, resigning from, or retiring from the role unless the individual formally and permanently ceases to hold the position. If the person vacates the role and then re-occupies the role, the contract may settle on the initial vacation of the role.

For "leave," cessation of holding the role qualifies, including resignation, retirement, removal, expulsion, expiration of term without renewal, recall, or other means by which the individual no longer occupies the role—this includes both voluntary and involuntary early departure AND the natural expiration of a term.

markets.rules_primary: If any member of Congress resigns or is expelled as any member of Congress in Nov 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Any member of Congress must have an actual departure date and vacate the role within the time period.

If the person leaves the role due to death (i.e., if the person dies while holding the role), all contracts on the person may resolve to the last fair price as determined in the sole discretion of the Exchange. Temporary leaves of absence, suspensions, or recusals do not constitute leaving, resigning from, or retiring from the role unless the individual formally and permanently ceases to hold the position. If the person vacates the role and then re-occupies the role, the contract may settle on the initial vacation of the role.

For "leave," cessation of holding the role qualifies, including resignation, retirement, removal, expulsion, expiration of term without renewal, recall, or other means by which the individual no longer occupies the role—this includes both voluntary and involuntary early departure AND the natural expiration of a term.

markets.rules_primary: If the United States Department of Commerce or the White House announces the designation of xAI as an AI national champion before Dec 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Only an announcement that expressly names the company counts: its own name, a former name, or an alias (a.k.a. or f.k.a.) listed in the announcement. The announcement may use the company's full legal name, such as Meta Platforms for Meta or Palantir Technologies for Palantir. A designation of Meta does not count for xAI, or the reverse, unless the announcement also names the other company itself or as an alias.

A designation counts when the Department of Commerce or the White House announces the company as an AI national champion, or as a member of a consortium or AI export package designated under the American AI Exports Program (also called the American SI Exports Program), in any official way, such as a press release, a posting on an official website or social media account, a statement at an official briefing or publication in the Federal Register, including in a list of designated companies.

The following do NOT count:
Coverage of the company only as an affiliate, subsidiary or parent of a designated company, including a designation that names only SpaceX for xAI
A designation that names only a different company, even one with a similar name
A report or statement that a designation is planned or expected but has not been announced
A contract, award, investment, export license or agreement that is not a designation under that program, or naming the company only as an applicant

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If James Talarico's margin of victory outperforms that of the Real Clear Polling average at 10 AM ET on Nov 3, 2026 in the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Texas, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market compares the official certified election result to the specified poll or polling average. "Outperform" means the actual result exceeds the poll figure; "underperform" means it falls short. Only certified results count - not preliminary tallies or projections. If using a poll range, the midpoint is used for comparison. Margins of error are not considered; any difference counts as over/underperformance.

For the purposes of this market, the Real Clear Polling average for the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Texas at 10 AM ET on November 3, 2026 is used to determine relative performance. At that time the average was Talarico 49.1%, Paxton 46.5% (Talarico +2.6), so James Talarico's polling margin is +2.6 points. James Talarico outperforms if the certified margin of victory is greater than +2.6 points.

For a winning candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate's vote share and their closest competitor's share. For a losing candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate’s vote share and the vote share of the candidate immediately ahead of them. Positive margins indicate the candidate won, negative margins indicate they lost, and zero indicates a tie. The polling margin is calculated the same way from the RCP Average figures, so a deficit in the average is a negative margin. Vote shares are percentages of all votes cast for the office.

Write-in votes are aggregated as a single candidate if not individually reported. Only certified results are used for resolution. Certification by the competent authority is the final result, even if later challenged, recounted, or litigated.

markets.rules_secondary: The margin of victory is calculated as the absolute difference in vote share (expressed as percentage) between first and second place finishers, using total votes cast as the denominator. For ranked-choice elections, the margin is the final-round vote difference between the first- and second-place candidates (the first round if a candidate wins a majority outright) divided by total votes cast in that election, including ballots exhausted before the final round. If official results aren't available by the deadline, preliminary results from Source Agencies with at least 95% of expected vote are used. If multiple elections have identical margins and relevant options are listed, each tied option resolves to Yes at $1.00 divided by the number of tied options.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the official vote count is certified.
markets.rules_primary: If at least 22,000,000 valid and null ballots are cast in the November 29, 2026 Spanish general election for the Congress of Deputies, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The count is the number of voters (votantes) for the Congress of Deputies: valid votes, including blank votes, plus null votes; registered voters, abstentions and Senate ballots do not count. If the Junta Electoral Central has not published national results by the Expiration Date, the count is the provincial electoral boards' general-scrutiny total, which includes votes from Spaniards resident abroad (CERA). The Ministry of the Interior's provisional count, which excludes CERA votes, is used only if the general scrutiny has not been completed in every province by the Expiration Date.

Subject to the contract’s Fully-Conducted Elections and Accelerated Resolution Upon Designated Media Source Declarations provisions, the vote count refers to the officially certified results from the relevant election authority. Provisional, absentee, early, mail-in, or electronic ballots are included only if reflected in the official certification.

The contract resolves based on officially certified results regardless of ongoing appeals. Outside those two contract provisions, preliminary counts, exit polls, projections, or uncertified results do not qualify. If the election is postponed but held within one year of the originally scheduled date, the contract remains valid; if postponed beyond one year or canceled before voting is fully conducted, all contracts resolve to No.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if complete Federal Register data becomes available.
markets.rules_primary: If the President signs above 0 executive orders during Nov 15, 2026 to Nov 21, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved

The signing date as recorded in the Federal Register determines which period an Executive Order belongs to.
For example, if the period was "Jan 1, 2025 to Jan 7, 2025," and on January 10th the Federal Register published a numbered Executive Order with a January 7th signing date, the market would resolve to Yes.

Payout criteria

An "Executive Order" is a numbered presidential directive that: is formally titled "Executive Order" followed by a number, is signed by the President, is published in the Federal Register, and has the force of law.
All documents officially designated as "Executive Orders" with sequential numbering count, including Executive Orders that are later revoked or amended.

Expiration date

The latest Expiration Date of the Contract shall be two weeks after the end of the period.
If an Executive Order that is dated past Nov 15, 2026 to Nov 21, 2026 is posted to the Federal Register, expiration may be moved to an earlier date.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the election results are certified.
markets.rules_primary: If Sherrod Brown's margin of victory outperforms that of the Real Clear Polling average at 10 AM ET on Nov 3, 2026 in the 2026 U.S. Senate special election in Ohio, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The market compares the official certified election result to the specified poll or polling average. "Outperform" means the actual result exceeds the poll figure; "underperform" means it falls short. Only certified results count - not preliminary tallies or projections. If using a poll range, the midpoint is used for comparison. Margins of error are not considered; any difference counts as over/underperformance.

For the purposes of this market, the Real Clear Polling average for the 2026 U.S. Senate special election in Ohio at 10 AM ET on November 3, 2026 is used to determine relative performance. At that time the average was Brown 48.5%, Husted 45.7% (Brown +2.8), so Sherrod Brown's polling margin is +2.8 points. Sherrod Brown outperforms if the certified margin of victory is greater than +2.8 points.

For a winning candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate's vote share and their closest competitor's share. For a losing candidate, the margin of victory is calculated as the difference between the candidate’s vote share and the vote share of the candidate immediately ahead of them. Positive margins indicate the candidate won, negative margins indicate they lost, and zero indicates a tie. The polling margin is calculated the same way from the RCP Average figures, so a deficit in the average is a negative margin. Vote shares are percentages of all votes cast for the office.

Write-in votes are aggregated as a single candidate if not individually reported. Only certified results are used for resolution. Certification by the competent authority is the final result, even if later challenged, recounted, or litigated.
markets.title: Will Sherrod Brown outperform the Real Clear Polling average in the 2026 U.S. Senate special election in Ohio?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the average U.S. wholesale price of whole chicken wings in November 2026 is above 85¢ per pound, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The November 2026 value will be the arithmetic mean of the “Wtd Avg” values initially published for “Wings – Whole” in each USDA Weekly National Chicken Report whose “Report For” period ends during November 2026.

The applicable figure appears under “Chicken, Parts – Domestic – Fresh – Conventional – FOB,” in the “Current Week’s Trading” columns, and is reported in cents per pound.

Each qualifying weekly value will receive equal weight. The “1,000 lbs” figures will not be used to reweight the weekly observations. No rounding will be applied to the calculated average before comparison with the strike.

If USDA does not publish a report for a particular week, no value will be imputed; the calculation will use all qualifying values that USDA publishes. Initially published values will be used regardless of later revisions, corrections, or updates.

Observation: Uses the closing index level of the one-minute candle ending Dec 4, 2026 at 10:15am EST: the S&P 500 value as of 10:14:59 AM EST on December 4, 2026, the preceding minute's final second. Each market compares that same observation with its stated fixed index-point strike. At least includes equality, which resolves Yes. Source Agencies (in priority order): S&P Dow Jones Indices, Pyth Network (official S&P 500 feeds), Bloomberg, WSJ, TradingView, Yahoo Finance, CNBC. If sources conflict, this order governs; any remaining dispute is resolved by Kalshi under Rule 7.1.

What counts as the S&P 500 value:
Only the index level calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices, to two decimal places.
ETFs, futures, options, perpetuals, and constituent stock prices do not count.
If no time of day is specified, the official closing value for each trading day is used. Intraday, open, high/low, and pre-/after-hours values do not count.

Trading days:
Only days with an official S&P 500 close count (Eastern Time). Weekends and market holidays are ignored.
If the specified observation is at or after an early close or a halt ending trading for the day, the official close designated by S&P Dow Jones Indices governs.

Index changes:
Changes to constituents, weightings, divisor, or methodology do not affect the contract.
If the index is renamed, rebranded, or re-coded but its record continues, the contract stays open. If it is discontinued with no successor, the No-data rule applies.

No data:
If no Source Agency publishes a value by the Expiration Date (including if markets are closed for the entire period), all markets resolve No, unless a "No data" strike is listed, in which case that strike resolves Yes.

Corrections:
Corrections published before Expiration govern; corrections published after Expiration are ignored.
If Kalshi finds a material error, it may delay Expiration until a corrected value is published. If none is published by the Expiration Date, the No-data rule applies.

Observation precision: If the exact-second index level is unavailable, the same-minute precision permitted by the contract applies. A different-time or stale price is not an automatic substitute.
